normalized.prelim_summary: This 1979 Volvo 262C Bertone coupe has been fitted with a more reliable 2.3L B230F engine and 4-speed overdrive manual from a 1988 Volvo 245, with recent suspension and brake work completed. It presents well cosmetically with a detailed interior and seller-provided videos, but lacks full documentation on the drivetrain swap's history and the original V6/wheels are not included. Bid to $10,750 with reserve not met.

contradictions.detail: The listing says the four-speed + OD (M46) came from the 1988 Volvo 245 donor. US 1988 240s used the M47 five-speed, and the seller conceded the gearbox origin is undocumented and may be separate.

critical_evidence.evidence: Only distant side and rear-3/4 shots of the roof and C-pillars were examined; no bubbling is visible at that scale. One lift photo covers the rear underside only. No close-ups of the vinyl roof edges, backlight surround, C-pillar bases, rockers or front fender bottoms were examined here.
No compression or leakdown numbers and no cooling-system pressure test. The donor engine's history is undocumented.

A BAR Vehicle Information Label (1/29/2026, 1988/Volvo/2.30L, manual, CA, matching VIN) is photographed, which supports the legal referee path. There are no swap receipts, no donor VIN or mileage proof, and no wiring or mount documentation, and the gearbox origin is uncertain.
The listing states a California title with a 'Title Only' notation. No title photo or DMV paperwork showing what is needed to register it was examined.

Brakes (pads, rotors, calipers, master cylinder), tie rods, springs, shocks, fan clutch, starter, battery, thermostat, cat (Jan 2026) and tires are all claimed with no invoices shown. The seller confirms no transmission service records.

documentation.rationale: The identity half is decent: the VIN is photographed on a BAR referee label matching the chassis, the swap configuration is certified, and a dated cat replacement is given. The maintenance half is missing: no invoices for any claimed work, no swap build records, no title photo, and no roof or C-pillar close-ups.

condition.rationale: Photos show glossy paint, a clean beige leather interior, and a dry, undercoated rear underside with only surface rust on the exhaust. Substantial chassis refresh work is claimed. On the negative side, radiator-support paint is flaking, the roof and C-pillar seams were not examined close, and there are no compression or cooling-system tests.

price_value.rationale: There are no comps or fair value to anchor against. Swapped 262Cs trade at a discount to V6 cars, and the Title Only notation and undocumented drivetrain narrow the buyer pool. The bid should land well inside the ideal band, but the value is only as good as the unseen roof and body.

mission_fit.rationale: It is manual and likely inexpensive, and the redblock/M46 is a durable, simple drivetrain. However, it is a 47-year-old niche coupe with 40+-year-old rubber throughout, no modern safety, a Title Only registration step and a thin resale pool. That is a weaker 6–24-month bridge than the Z3 3.0i targets.

logistics.rationale: It is a California car in Montclair (~5–6 hours from Carmel) with a BAR label and a claimed smog pass, sold by a responsive dealer consignor. PPI access before the Oct 1 close is unconfirmed, and the Title Only registration process adds DMV steps.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: A rare Bertone body with a manual overdrive and nice beige leather are genuine positives. They are offset by the lost original PRV drivetrain, a respray of unknown provenance, a donor 245 dash, whitewalls, an aftermarket wheel and non-original wheels.

positives: The BAR referee label (1/29/2026, VIN-matched) shows the redblock swap went through the California referee process, and the seller reports a smog pass.
The durable B230F/LH2.2 four and M46 overdrive manual are simpler and more robust than the PRV V6 with CIS; the seller says the OD engages properly.

Substantial recent chassis work is claimed: full brakes including master cylinder, tie rods, springs, shocks, fan clutch, thermostat, starter, battery, cat (Jan 2026) and tires.
The rear underside lift photo shows an undercoated, dry floor and axle area with only surface rust on the exhaust.
The dealer consignor is responsive and candid about documentation gaps.

evidence.mission_note: It meets the manual requirement and should sell well inside the ideal price band, but it is a 47-year-old niche Bertone coupe with a non-original drivetrain and a Title Only notation. As a 6–24-month enthusiast bridge it is an off-list curiosity, not a substitute for the Z3 3.0i targets.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes identity well: the chassis VIN matches a photographed BAR referee label dated 1/29/2026 certifying a 1988 2.3L manual configuration, which supports California legality of the redblock swap. It also documents a presentable car in photos: glossy gold paint, clean beige leather, and a rear underside showing only surface rust on the exhaust. Observed issues are the 'Title Only' notation on the California title, an undocumented swap (donor mileage is hearsay and the M46 cannot have come from a US 1988 245 as stated), a pre-2025 respray of unknown reason, and flaking paint on the radiator support. Extensive work since 2025 is claimed, including brakes, master cylinder, tie rods, springs, shocks, fan clutch, thermostat, starter, cat and tires, but no invoices are shown. The model-critical 262C risk areas remain open: close-ups of the vinyl roof edges, C-pillar bases, backlight surround and rockers were not examined here, and there is no compression or cooling test. There are no comps, so value depends almost entirely on the unseen roof and body. The seller has been candid and responsive, which makes these gaps answerable before the Thursday close.
